long_biography.plain_text:
Born in Los Angeles in 1960, Eric Smidt endured an unsettled childhood and moved into his own apartment at 16. A year later he and his father, Allan, started Harbor Freight as a small North Hollywood mail-order tool business. Smidt became president in 1985, bought out his father's stake in 1999 and became sole owner, making his fortune self-made rather than inherited.

He built the retailer around direct factory sourcing and lower-priced tools, then expanded it across the United States. Harbor Freight now describes more than 1,600 stores and 26,000 associates, while Forbes estimates nearly $9 billion in annual sales. Smidt remains owner and chief executive. His foundation's flagship Harbor Freight Tools for Schools program funds skilled-trades education. His maritime record is unusually continuous: public reports connect him to two successive yachts named Infinity and the support vessel Intrepid.
